The primary mechanism is the exploitation of asynchronous concurrency, where the CPU performs memory operations while the GPU simultaneously executes data transfers, thereby hiding the transfer time behind the computation time. This reduces overall latency because the total execution time becomes the maximum of the individual operation durations rather than their sum, effectively parallelizing tasks that would otherwise occur sequentially. Consequently, the system avoids idle waiting periods for either the CPU or the GPU, leading to more efficient utilization of hardware resources and faster model loading or inference startup.
